summary: This Dockerfile creates a container that runs a lightweight desktop environment (Lubuntu) with a display manager (LightDM). It configures LightDM to connect to an X server running on the host machine rather than creating one inside the container, and sets everything up to auto-login and display graphically on the host.

explanations.3: The && operator chains commands so that apt-get install only runs if apt-get update succeeds. DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive tells the installer not to prompt for user input, which is necessary in unattended Docker builds.
explanations.4: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists (in /var/lib/apt/lists) to reduce the Docker image size, since those files aren't needed once installation is done.
explanations.6: This removes any lingering reboot-required marker files that the package installer might have created, since containers can't actually reboot.
explanations.7: This tells LightDM which display manager executable to use; the file /etc/X11/default-display-manager is where the system looks for this configuration.
explanations.19: This environment variable tells GUI applications where to find the X display server; host.docker.internal is Docker's way of referring to the host machine's network address.
explanations.21: CMD specifies what runs when the container starts: it launches the dbus message bus (needed for system services) and then starts the LightDM display manager.
